3.happening: The verdict starts from the length comparison.
3.why: Anagrams must contain the same number of characters.
3.invariant: answer is false immediately when lengths differ.

4.happening: The algorithm checks the initial length verdict.
4.why: A false verdict needs no character scanning.
4.invariant: Only equal-length strings reach the nested scans.

5.happening: The false length verdict is returned.
5.invariant: answer accurately represents the rejected input.

6.happening: Every character in t starts unused.
6.why: Each source character must claim a distinct matching position.
6.invariant: used[j] is true only after t[j] has been consumed.

7.happening: Start with the first source character.
7.why: This establishes the state needed for the exhaustive search.
7.invariant: Initialization preserves the problem input and prepares valid working state.

8.why: The brute-force method must enumerate every relevant candidate.
8.invariant: No candidate in the current search range is skipped.

9.happening: Assume no match has been found yet.
9.why: This establishes the state needed for the exhaustive search.
9.invariant: Initialization preserves the problem input and prepares valid working state.

10.happening: Start scanning t from the beginning.
10.why: This establishes the state needed for the exhaustive search.
10.invariant: Initialization preserves the problem input and prepares valid working state.

11.why: The brute-force method must enumerate every relevant candidate.
11.invariant: No candidate in the current search range is skipped.

12.why: The brute-force scan checks candidates one by one.
12.invariant: Candidates before j were unavailable or different.

13.happening: Check whether the candidate is unused.
13.why: The working state must reflect the candidate or result just discovered.
13.invariant: Recorded state remains consistent with all work completed so far.

14.happening: Accept only an equal unused candidate.
14.why: This condition decides whether the current candidate can contribute to the answer.
14.invariant: Only candidates satisfying the algorithm's condition advance.

15.happening: t[{j}] is consumed as the match for s[{i}].
15.why: The same target character cannot satisfy two source characters.

16.happening: Record that this source character matched.
16.why: The working state must reflect the candidate or result just discovered.
16.invariant: Recorded state remains consistent with all work completed so far.

17.happening: Stop scanning t for this source character.
17.why: This value reports the completed branch or final answer.
17.invariant: The returned value matches all candidates explored by this scope.

18.happening: Advance to the next t candidate.
18.why: Advancing the pointer continues the exhaustive scan.
18.invariant: The pointer moves within its valid range.

19.happening: Check whether the full t scan failed.
19.why: This condition decides whether the current candidate can contribute to the answer.
19.invariant: Only candidates satisfying the algorithm's condition advance.

20.happening: No unused match exists for s[{i}].
20.why: The strings cannot contain the same character multiset.

21.happening: The false matching verdict is returned.
21.why: One unmatched source character disproves an anagram.

22.happening: Advance to the next source character.
22.why: Advancing the pointer continues the exhaustive scan.
22.invariant: The pointer moves within its valid range.

23.happening: Every source character found a distinct match.
23.why: Equal lengths plus one-to-one matches prove an anagram.

init.happening: Reset source and candidate scan state.
init.why: Each source character begins a fresh search through t.
init.invariant: Previously consumed t positions stay marked.

loop.happening: Scan another source character or candidate.
loop.why: Brute force may inspect all n candidates for each source.

check.happening: Test lengths, a candidate pair, or scan failure.
check.why: Only an equal unused candidate is valid.

update.happening: Compare or consume a matching character.
update.why: The used row records the partial pairing.
update.invariant: A consumed target position never becomes free again.

move.happening: Advance a source or candidate pointer.
move.why: Nested scans cover every possible pairing.

return.why: A missing match rejects; complete pairing accepts.
